pit_brackets_short: 0% up to €12,348; 14–42% (geometric progression); 42% from €69,879; 45% from €277,826; + solidarity surcharge 5.5% of the tax (high incomes) and church tax 8–9% of the tax
foreign_income_note: residents are taxed on worldwide income; for business — municipal trade tax (Gewerbesteuer)
residency_rule: housing at one's disposal in Germany or habitual stay >6 months (including continuously across the turn of the year)
self_employed_regime: no special income-tax regime (general scale); Kleinunternehmer is only a VAT exemption for small turnover; trade tax (threshold €24,500) is for trade/crafts, Freiberufler do not pay it
expat_regime: no
cbi_note: no citizenship or residence permit for buying property; residence permit only through business/investment (business plan, economic interest), citizenship — naturalization

pit_brackets_short: 10/14/20/31/35/47% + 3% surcharge above ILS 721,560 (50% in total); a further +2% on capital income above the threshold
foreign_income_note: residents are taxed on worldwide income; new repatriates and those returning after 10+ years — 10 years of exemption for foreign income
residency_rule: centre of vital interests; rebuttable presumption: 183+ days in a year or 30+ days in a year and 425+ days over 3 years
self_employed_regime: no special regime; self-employed on the general scale
expat_regime: olim and those returning after 10+ years: 10 years of exemption on foreign passive and business income; for those who became residents 05.11.2025–31.12.2026 — exemption of Israeli employment/business income up to ILS 600,000 (2026), 1 million (2027–2028), 350,000 (2029), 150,000 (2030); those arriving from 2026 are required to declare foreign income
cbi_note: there are no citizenship/residence permit programmes for investment or real estate; citizenship — Law of Return or naturalization

pit_brackets_short: 19/24/30/37/45/47% (state + regional parts, differs by region); savings income 19–30%
foreign_income_note: residents are taxed on worldwide income; rates depend on the autonomous community; exemption up to €60,100 for work abroad
residency_rule: >183 days in a calendar year or centre of economic interests in Spain (presumption if the family is in Spain)
self_employed_regime: no special tax regime (autónomo — general scale); autónomo social contributions 31.4% of the chosen base (€653.59–5,101.20/month)
expat_regime: Beckham regime (art. 93 LIRPF as amended by Ley 28/2022): 24% on income up to €600,000 (above that 47%), 6 years (year of move + 5), if not a resident in the 5 previous years; foreign passive income is mostly not taxed under the regime. For remote work — only for employees (trabajadores por cuenta ajena) with a teletrabajo visa; the self-employed — only as entrepreneurs under an ENISA report or startup/R&D specialists. Not available to a self-employed person with foreign clients: scale 19–47% + RETA
cbi_note: residence permit only, and that is closed: the "golden visa" for real estate (€500,000) was abolished from 3 April 2025; those issued earlier are renewed; no citizenship by investment

pit_brackets_short: 0% up to AUD 18,200; 16/30/37/45% + Medicare levy 2%
foreign_income_note: residents are taxed on worldwide income; temporary residents (temporary visa, no Australian spouse) are exempt from tax on foreign income
residency_rule: domicile in Australia or 183+ days in a year (if the usual place of residence is not abroad); ordinary residence test
self_employed_regime: no special regime; general scale
expat_regime: temporary residents do not pay tax on foreign income and most foreign capital gains; working holiday — 15% on the first AUD 45,000
cbi_note: no citizenship or residence permit for buying real estate; the SIV investor visa is closed, the route is NIV 858 for distinguished entrepreneurs/investors (permanent residence), citizenship after 4 years

foreign_income_note: residents are taxed on worldwide income
residency_rule: availability of housing (Wohnsitz) or stay >6 months
self_employed_regime: basic flat-rate scheme: from 2026 expenses are recognised at 15% of turnover (up to €63,000) with turnover up to €420,000; also a flat-rate scheme for small entrepreneurs
expat_regime: Zuzugsbegünstigung — only for invited scientists/researchers, artists and athletes: exemption of 30% of income from scientific activity for 5 years; for scientists, artists, athletes — a fixed average rate (min. 15%) on foreign income; application within 6 months, public interest required. Not available to the self-employed: worldwide income on a 20–55% scale
cbi_note: no citizenship or residence permit for real estate; citizenship under §10(6) for "exceptional merit" (including large business investments, at the government's discretion), not for buying housing

pit_brackets_short: private non-oil sector (monthly): 3% up to AZN 2,500, 10% up to 8,000, 14% above (3%→5% in 2027, 7% from 2028); oil and gas and public sector: 14%/25% (above AZN 2,500/month)
foreign_income_note: residents are taxed on worldwide income; the 7-year exemption for private-sector salaries ended in 2025, with a phased increase from 2026
residency_rule: >182 days in a calendar year; otherwise — place of permanent residence, centre of vital interests, citizenship
self_employed_regime: simplified tax 2% of revenue for sole proprietors/companies without VAT with turnover up to AZN 200,000 over 12 months (certain types — 6–8%)
expat_regime: no
cbi_note: residence permit only: real estate from ~$60,000 gives a 1-year residence permit with renewal; permanent residence after 2 years; citizenship — naturalization (5+ years)

pit_top_threshold: ARS 60,750,914 (1st half of 2026; indexed every six months)
foreign_income_note: residents are taxed on worldwide income with credit for foreign tax; also personal property tax 0.5–1% (for "bona fide" 0–0.5%) above the threshold
residency_rule: foreigners — residents after 12 months of stay or 5 years of work; seconded <5 years — non-residents
self_employed_regime: monotributo: a single fixed monthly payment (tax + social contributions) at annual turnover up to ~ARS 126.6 million (cat. K, 2nd half of 2026)
expat_regime: foreigners posted to work for <5 years are non-residents (tax only on Argentine income); obtaining citizenship by investment does not by itself make one a tax resident
cbi_note: a citizenship-by-investment programme has been created (decrees 366/2025, 524/2025), but is not launched for 2026: the amounts (~$500,000 under discussion) and the eligibility of real estate are not approved; investor residence permit suspended

pit_brackets_short: 20% flat; dividends 5%, rent and royalties 10%
foreign_income_note: residents are taxed on worldwide income
residency_rule: 183+ days in a calendar year or centre of life interests in Armenia
self_employed_regime: microbusiness 0% with turnover up to AMD 24 million (from 07.2025 excluding consulting, IT, advertising, translation); turnover tax for sole proprietors (IE) 1–12% (trade 10%, production 7%) with turnover up to AMD 115 million
expat_regime: no
cbi_note: no citizenship/residence permit for buying real estate; residence permit via sole proprietorship/business with no minimum investment

pit_brackets_short: 25/40/45/50% + municipal surcharge 0–9% of the tax (on average ~7%)
foreign_income_note: residents are taxed on worldwide income; interest and dividend income — 30%
residency_rule: domicile or centre of economic interests in Belgium, or registration in the commune
self_employed_regime: no special personal income tax regime
expat_regime: regime for newcomers (BNI/BRI): tax-free compensation of 35% of salary (since 2025), no limit, 5 years + extension of 3; salary from €70,000 (no minimum for researchers); not a resident for 60 months, lived >150 km from the border, application within 3 months
cbi_note: no citizenship or residence permit for real estate; business residence permit with investment of ~€350,000–500,000 in a company

pit_brackets_short: 10% flat; dividends 5%
foreign_income_note: residents are taxed on worldwide income; interest on deposits in the EU/EEA is not taxed
residency_rule: permanent address and centre of interests in Bulgaria, or >183 days in any 12 months
self_employed_regime: liberal professions: standard expense deduction 25% (40% for authors, lawyers) → effectively 7.5%; self-employed social contributions ~27.8% with a ceiling of €2,300/month (from 08.2026)
expat_regime: no
cbi_note: residence permit only: real estate from ~€307,000 (+ account ≥€7,443); permanent residence after 5 years, citizenship after 10 with renunciation of the previous one; the citizenship-by-investment programme was abolished

pit_brackets_short: Federation of BiH 10%, Republika Srpska 8%, Brčko District 10%
foreign_income_note: residents of the FBiH and Brčko are taxed on worldwide income; in RS foreign income is taxed in fixed amounts
residency_rule: place of residence or 183+ days in a year (FBiH) / in 12 months (RS)
self_employed_regime: Republika Srpska: small entrepreneurs — 2% of annual revenue
expat_regime: no
cbi_note: residence permit only: property ownership is mentioned as a basis for a temporary residence permit (1 year with extension), amount not set; no citizenship by investment

pit_brackets_short: 0/7.5/15/22.5/27.5% (monthly); from 2026 income up to BRL 5,000/month is effectively exempt (the reduction phases out up to BRL 7,350); minimum tax of up to 10% on income > BRL 600,000/year; 10% withholding on dividends > BRL 50,000/month.
foreign_income_note: residents are taxed on worldwide income; since 2024 foreign financial income and profits of controlled offshore entities — 15% (law 14.754/2023)
residency_rule: 183 days of presence in 12 months (temporary visa without an employment contract); permanent residence holders and work visa holders with a Brazilian contract — from entry
self_employed_regime: self-employed: INSS 5/11/20% of the base; MEI and Simples Nacional — simplified regimes for small business
expat_regime: no
cbi_note: residence permit only: real estate from BRL 1 million (BRL 700,000 in the north/northeast) gives permanent residence; citizenship — naturalization (usually 4 years)

foreign_income_note: from 6.04.2025 non-dom and the remittance basis were abolished; residents are taxed on worldwide income (newcomers — see the FIG regime, 4 years)
residency_rule: Statutory Residence Test: automatically resident with 183+ days, the only home in the UK for 91+ days or full-time work in the UK; otherwise — ties test + days
self_employed_regime: no special regime: general scale + Class 4 NIC 6% (£12,570–50,270) and 2% above
expat_regime: FIG regime: 4 years of exemption of foreign income and capital gains for those who were not resident in the 10 preceding years; + overseas workday relief (up to £300,000 or 30% of salary)
cbi_note: no citizenship or residence permit for real estate (Tier 1 Investor closed in 2022); citizenship — naturalization (ILR + 1 year, usually 6 years)

pit_brackets_short: 15% flat
foreign_income_note: residents are taxed on worldwide income (foreign income with credit under DTA)
residency_rule: Hungarian citizen / permanent residence; or the only permanent home or centre of vital interests in Hungary; otherwise 183+ days in a calendar year
self_employed_regime: KATA: HUF 50,000/month fixed with revenue up to HUF 18 million, only for sole proprietors selling to private individuals (not companies)
expat_regime: no
cbi_note: residence permit only: Guest Investor (since 2024) — €250,000 in a real estate fund or €1 million donation; direct purchase of housing excluded since 1.03.2024. Citizenship — naturalization 8 years

pit_brackets_short: 5/10/20/30/35% (new 5-bracket scale for salaries: 120/360/720/1 200 million VND); non-residents — flat 20%
foreign_income_note: residents — worldwide income wherever paid; non-residents — only Vietnamese-source income
residency_rule: 183+ days in a calendar year or over 12 months from the date of entry, or permanent housing (registration/lease) in Vietnam
self_employed_regime: business household: income up to VND 1 billion/year is exempt from PIT; above that — 15–20% of net profit (or % of revenue)
expat_regime: no
cbi_note: neither citizenship nor residence permit for real estate; residence permit via business investment (DT1–DT3, from ~$125,000), citizenship — naturalization from 5 years

pit_brackets_short: 9/20/26/34/39/44% (step €10,000, 39% up to €60,000); reduced scales for children and under 30; rental 15–45%
foreign_income_note: residents — worldwide income; there are preferential regimes 5A/5B/5C
residency_rule: stay of more than 183 days in any 12 months or centre of life interests in Greece
self_employed_regime: no special regime: freelancers on the general scale 9–44% + EFKA contributions
expat_regime: 5A: 50% exemption of salary/income for 7 years for those moving to work; 5B non-dom: €100,000/year flat on foreign income for up to 15 years with investments of €500,000; 5C: pensioners 7% on foreign income
cbi_note: residence permit only: Golden Visa — €800,000 (Attica, Thessaloniki, Mykonos, Santorini, large islands), €400,000 other regions, €250,000 conversion/restoration; short-term rental is prohibited. Citizenship — naturalization 7 years (the Golden Visa does not give residence credit without living there)

pit_brackets_short: 20% flat
foreign_income_note: residents are exempt from tax on income not from Georgia
residency_rule: 183+ days in Georgia in any continuous 12-month period ending in the current year; or HNWI status
self_employed_regime: small business: 1% of turnover up to GEL 500,000 (3% above); micro business up to GEL 30,000 — 0%
expat_regime: HNWI residency without 183 days: assets > GEL 3 million or income > GEL 200,000 over 3 years + real estate in Georgia from $500,000 (or a residence permit / Georgian income of GEL 25,000); foreign income is not taxed anyway
cbi_note: residence permit only: real estate from $150,000 (from 1.03.2026, previously $100,000) — 1-year residence permit; from $300,000 — investment residence permit for 5 years. Citizenship — 10 years, with renunciation of the previous one

pit_brackets_short: state: bottom 12.01% + middle 7.5% (>DKK 696,956) + top 7.5% (>DKK 845,543) + top-top 5%; + municipal ~25% + AM 8%; cap ~60.5%
foreign_income_note: fully tax-resident — worldwide income; plus municipal tax ~25% (average 25.049%) and church tax ~0.6%
residency_rule: housing in Denmark (purchase/rental) with the intention to stay, or 6 months of continuous stay — taxation from day one
self_employed_regime: no special regime (per PwC data)
expat_regime: regime for researchers/key employees: 27% of gross salary + AM 8% (total 32.84%) for up to 84 months, salary from DKK 65,400/month
cbi_note: neither citizenship nor residence permit for real estate; foreigners need Ministry of Justice sanction to buy housing. Citizenship — 9 years

pit_brackets_short: 0% up to DOP 416,220 / 15 / 20 / 25%; from 2027 — a new 27% bracket above DOP 4.8 million
foreign_income_note: foreign income is not taxed, except investment and financial income of residents — after 3 years of residency
residency_rule: more than 182 days in a calendar year (consecutive or not)
expat_regime: no
cbi_note: residence permit only: investor residency from $200,000 (Dirección General de Migración; Decree 631-11, art. 55); then accelerated naturalisation (Law 1683)

pit_brackets_short: 0% up to EGP 40,000 / 10 / 15 / 20 / 22.5 / 25 / 27.5%; + personal allowance EGP 20,000
foreign_income_note: residents — total income, including worldwide, if the centre of commercial activity is in Egypt; non-residents — Egyptian-source
residency_rule: permanent housing in Egypt or more than 183 days in 12 months
self_employed_regime: simplified regime (Law 6/2025): 0.4–1.5% of turnover for small business with revenue up to EGP 20 million
expat_regime: no
cbi_min_amount: USD 300,000 (state real estate, hold for 5 years)
cbi_note: the programme is operating (36 passports in 2025); alternatives: donation $250,000, deposit $500,000 for 3 years, business $350,000 + $100,000; from 2025 — mandatory visits (2 days at filing, ~4 weeks after approval); acceptance of Syrians suspended. Residence permit for real estate — from $50,000

pit_brackets_short: new regime: 0% up to INR 400,000 / 5/10/15/20/25/30%; + surcharge 10–25% above INR 5 million + cess 4%; 100% rebate at income up to INR 1.2 million
foreign_income_note: ROR — worldwide income; RNOR and non-residents — Indian-source only
residency_rule: 182+ days in a year or 60+ days in a year and 365+ days in the previous 4 years; RNOR — non-resident 9 of 10 years or ≤729 days in 7 years
expat_regime: RNOR status for newcomers (non-resident 9 out of 10 years or ≤729 days over 7 years): foreign income is not taxed
cbi_note: neither citizenship nor residence permit for real estate; citizenship — 12 years of residence, dual citizenship prohibited

pit_brackets_short: 5/15/25/30/35% (60 million / 250 million / 500 million / 5 billion IDR); non-residents — 20% WHT
foreign_income_note: residents — worldwide income; foreign specialists — only Indonesian-source income for the first 4 years
residency_rule: residence in Indonesia, or more than 183 days in 12 months, or presence in the year with the intention to reside
self_employed_regime: PPh Final UMKM: 0.5% of turnover up to IDR 4.8 billion for individuals/sole proprietors (PP 20/2026, indefinite); turnover up to IDR 500 million — 0%
expat_regime: qualified foreign experts: 4 years of taxation on Indonesian-source income only (Omnibus Law)
cbi_note: residence permit only: Second Home Visa (5 years, extendable once to 10 years) — IDR 2 billion in a bank account or a property ownership certificate (Immigration Directorate General, immigration office guidance); Golden Visa via government bonds, listed-company shares or deposits, or by establishing a company (Directorate General of Immigration). Citizenship — naturalization with renunciation of the previous one

pit_brackets_short: 20/40% + USC 0.5–8% (11% for self-employed above €100,000) + PRSI
foreign_income_note: residents and domiciled — worldwide income; residents without Irish domicile — foreign income only when remitted to Ireland
residency_rule: 183+ days in a year or 280+ days over 2 years (minimum 30 in each)
self_employed_regime: no special regime: general scale + USC + PRSI Class S
expat_regime: SARP: 30% of income above €125,000 exempt (maximum €1 million), 5 years, for newcomers assigned by an employer until 2030; + remittance basis for non-dom
cbi_note: neither citizenship nor residence permit for real estate; the IIP programme was closed in February 2023. Citizenship — 5 years of residence

foreign_income_note: residents — worldwide income; + taxes on foreign real estate (IVIE 1.06%) and assets (IVAFE 0.2%)
residency_rule: more than 183 days in a year: registration in Anagrafe, or habitual abode, or domicile (centre of interests) / physical presence
self_employed_regime: forfettario: 15% on deemed profit with revenue up to €85,000; the 5% rate (start-up) does not apply when continuing the same activity carried out abroad (AE, risposta 197/2022); effectively ≈ 11.7% of revenue + INPS
expat_regime: impatriati: 50% income exemption (60% with a child), limit €600,000/year, 5 years, not a resident for 3+ years, high qualification, 4-year commitment; flat tax €300,000/year on foreign income (from 2026); pensioners in the south — 7% for 10 years
cbi_note: neither citizenship nor residence permit for real estate; the Investor Visa has no real estate option. Citizenship — 10 years

pit_brackets_short: 10% up to 8,500 MCI / 15% above (from 2026, new Tax Code)
foreign_income_note: residents are taxed on worldwide income, non-residents — only on Kazakhstani income; there are no local income taxes
residency_rule: 183+ days in any rolling 12-month period or centre of vital interests in the Czech Republic
self_employed_regime: Sole proprietor (IE) on the simplified declaration: 4% of income (maslikhats may change within 2–6%), limit 600,000 MRP (~KZT 2.6 billion) per year, not a VAT payer; plus the IE's own social contributions from the minimum wage
expat_regime: no
cbi_note: no citizenship by investment, dual citizenship is prohibited. Only a residence permit: investment from $300,000 in charter capital of Kazakh companies or domestic securities (investor visa, "golden visa", residence permit up to 10 years) (Otandastar Foundation page on the Ministry of Foreign Affairs rules); citizenship by naturalization after 5 years

pit_brackets_short: federal 14/20.5/26/29/33% + provincial up to 11.5–25.75% → combined top ~44.5–54.8%
foreign_income_note: residents — on worldwide income; besides federal tax there is provincial/territorial (top from 11.5% Nunavut to 25.75% Quebec); AMT 20.5%
residency_rule: 183+ days in a calendar year (deemed resident) or strong ties (housing, family, economic ties)
self_employed_regime: no special regime; self-employed pay CPP at double rate (employee and employer share), EI voluntary. Employee contributions 2026: CPP up to CAD 4,646, EI up to CAD 1,123 per year
expat_regime: no
cbi_note: no citizenship/residence permit for real estate; foreigners are prohibited from buying residential property (ban extended to 01.01.2027). Permanent residence via provincial business/investment programmes (e.g. Quebec), citizenship — 3 of 5 years of physical presence after permanent residence

foreign_income_note: residents — on worldwide income; non-domiciled are exempt from SDC (defence tax) on dividends, interest, rent for 17 of 20 years; SDC on dividends from 2026 — 5%
residency_rule: more than 183 days in a calendar year, or the 60-day rule: ≥60 days in Cyprus, not >183 days in another country, work/business/directorship in a Cypriot company and owned/rented housing
self_employed_regime: no special regime; the self-employed pay social insurance 16.6% + GESY 4% (≈20.6%) of income within limits
expat_regime: non-dom: SDC exemption on dividends/interest for 17 years; 50% exemption of salary >€55,000 for 17 years (not a resident for 15 years before hiring); 20% exemption up to €8,550/year for 7 years; new 25% exemption up to €25,000/year (2025–2030, income >€30,000, 7 years)
cbi_note: the citizenship by investment programme was closed in 2020 and not restored; accelerated citizenship for holders of investor permanent residence was abolished. Residence permit only: permanent residence (Reg. 6(2)) for buying new real estate from €300,000 + income ≥€50,000/year; citizenship by naturalization after 7 years + Greek B1

pit_brackets_short: 3/10/20/25/30/35/45% (aggregate income); business income 5–35%; passive income 20%
foreign_income_note: residents are taxed on worldwide income, but foreigners are exempt from tax on foreign income for the first 6 years (6-year rule, reset by leaving for >30 consecutive days); no local income taxes
residency_rule: domicile in China or 183+ days in the tax year
self_employed_regime: income from business activity 5–35% progressive (from CNY 30,000 … above CNY 500,000)
expat_regime: 6-year rule for foreign income; for foreigners part of the compensation (housing, children's education, language) is not taxed — extended to the end of 2027; in Hainan, the Greater Bay Area (GBA) and Hengqin a tax refund above 15% for talents until 2027
cbi_note: no citizenship by investment/real estate, dual citizenship is prohibited, naturalization is extremely rare. Only investment-based permanent residence (from ~$500,000 into a business) — rare

foreign_income_note: tax residents (including foreigners) are taxed on worldwide income, non-residents — on Colombian income; no local income taxes
residency_rule: 183 days in any period of 365 consecutive days (for citizens — also income/assets/family criteria)
self_employed_regime: Régimen SIMPLE (RST): a single tax on gross revenue with income <100,000 UVT; for professional services/consulting 7.3–8.3%
expat_regime: no
cbi_note: there is no citizenship by investment. Residence permit only: investor visa M for real estate from 350 SMMLV (~COP 613 million), resident visa R from 650 SMMLV; naturalization after 5 years with visa R, dual citizenship allowed

pit_top_threshold: salary: ₡4,727,000 per month; self-employed: ₡20,442,000 per year
foreign_income_note: only income from sources in Costa Rica is taxed, regardless of residency; foreign income is not taxed
residency_rule: more than 183 days in the fiscal year (consecutive or with breaks)
self_employed_regime: no special regime; self-employed — progressive scale 0–25% and CCSS contributions
expat_regime: territorial system; digital nomad regime (law 10008): income from foreign employers is not taxed
cbi_note: no citizenship by investment. Residence permit only: temporary investor residence permit for real estate from $150,000 (reduced from $200,000), permanent residence after 3 years, citizenship by naturalisation after 7 years

pit_brackets_short: 10% flat
foreign_income_note: only citizens of the KR who are tax residents are taxed on worldwide income; foreigners and non-residents — only on income from the KR; no local income taxes
residency_rule: 183+ days in any 12-month period ending in the tax year
self_employed_regime: Sole proprietor (IE) on the simplified regime: single tax 4% (non-cash) / 6% (cash); HTP (High-Tech Park) for IT: 1% of revenue to the HTP fund, exemption from profit tax/sales tax/VAT, employees' personal income tax 5% — the regime has been made indefinite
expat_regime: no (except tax benefits of the Hi-Tech Park for IT)
cbi_note: no citizenship by investment/real estate (Tranio: only standard naturalization). Only an investor residence permit from $100,000 (National Investment Agency); naturalization after 5 years

pit_brackets_short: 25.5% up to €105,300 / 33% above + additional 3% on income above €200,000
foreign_income_note: residents — on worldwide income; dividends from profit taxed with corporate tax are exempt (except the 3% surcharge)
residency_rule: declared place of residence, or 183+ days in any 12-month period
self_employed_regime: micro-enterprise tax (MUN) 25% of turnover (up to the VAT registration threshold, minimum €50/year) instead of PIT and social contributions; self-employed on the general regime — social contributions 31.07%
expat_regime: no
cbi_note: no citizenship by investment. Residence permit for real estate (€250,000 in Riga/Jūrmala) terminated from 15.09.2026; replacement — a €150,000 deposit in a fund for 5 years + €10,000 (mechanism ~by 2027). Naturalization 10 years

pit_brackets_short: salary 20/32%; other income 15/20% (threshold €253,065); dividends 15%; individual activity 5–15%
foreign_income_note: residents — on worldwide income; non-residents — only on certain types of Lithuanian income
residency_rule: permanent place of residence or centre of interests in Lithuania, or 183+ days in a year (or 280 days over 2 years)
self_employed_regime: individual activity: 15% with credit → effectively 5–15%, social contributions 19.5% of 90% of income; business certificate — fixed tax, social contributions 15.7% of the minimum wage
expat_regime: no
cbi_note: no citizenship by investment; no residence permit for buying real estate (only via business/work); naturalization 10 years

pit_brackets_short: 8–42% (many brackets) + solidarity tax 7% / 9% of the tax → max. ~45.78%
foreign_income_note: residents — on worldwide income; solidarity surcharge 7% (9% with income >€150,000 class 1); tax classes 1/1a/2
residency_rule: dwelling actually used in Luxembourg or a stay of more than 6 consecutive months
self_employed_regime: no special regime
expat_regime: impatriate regime (from 2025): 50% exemption of remuneration up to €400,000/year, base salary ≥€75,000, not a resident/not lived within 150 km of the border for 5 years, for the year of arrival + 8 years
cbi_note: no citizenship by investment; real estate does not count even for an investor residence permit (€500,000 in a business / €20 million deposit); citizenship by naturalisation after 5 years

foreign_income_note: income sourced in Malaysia is taxed; foreign income brought in by a resident is exempt from 2022 until 31.12.2036 (under conditions); no local income taxes
residency_rule: 182+ days in a calendar year
self_employed_regime: no special regime; general progressive scale
expat_regime: foreign income exempt until 2036; 15% rate for the Returning Expert Programme (5 years), Iskandar knowledge workers, C-suite; 15% proposed in Forest City SFZ
cbi_note: no citizenship by investment. Only the MM2H residence permit: Silver deposit $150,000 + property from RM 600,000 (5 years), Gold $500,000 + RM 1 million (15 years), Platinum $1 million + RM 2 million (20 years); buying housing is mandatory, no direct path to citizenship

foreign_income_note: domiciled residents are taxed on worldwide income; non-domiciled residents — Maltese income + foreign income remitted to Malta; minimum tax €5,000 if unremitted foreign income is ≥€35,000
residency_rule: ordinary residence (ordinarily resident) — living in Malta in the ordinary course; domicile — by the place of the permanent home
self_employed_regime: self-employed — social contributions 15% (max €83.89/week); side work/partial self-employment — 10% (with a limit)
expat_regime: Highly Qualified Persons 15% (salary ≥€65,000, up to 15 years); Global Residence Programme 15% on foreign income brought in (min. €15,000/year); Nomad Residence Permit 10%; remittance basis for non-dom
cbi_note: the citizenship by investment programme (included buying real estate from €700,000 or renting at €16,000/year) was closed after the CJEU ruling of 29.04.2025, Act XXI of 2025; replacement — discretionary citizenship "for merit" with no price. Residence permit only: MPRP / real estate purchase from €375,000 or rent from €14,000 per year (Residency Malta Agency), citizenship by naturalisation ≥15 years

pit_brackets_short: 1.92–35% (11 brackets); dividends 10%, exchange capital gains 10%
foreign_income_note: residents are taxed on worldwide income; non-residents — only Mexican-source income (salary 15–30%)
residency_rule: a home (house) in Mexico; if there is a home in another country too — centre of vital interests (>50% of income from Mexico or main professional activity)
self_employed_regime: RESICO: 1–2.5% of turnover without deductions at income up to MXN 3.5 million/year (residents only)
expat_regime: no
cbi_note: residence permit only: temporary residence permit (up to 4 years) for real estate valued above 91,710 UMA days (Secretariat of Foreign Affairs, embassy guidance), permanent residence after 4 years (Migration Law, art. 54), citizenship by naturalization after 5 years + exam (Secretariat of Foreign Affairs)

pit_brackets_short: 12% (dividends 6%, capital gains 12%)
foreign_income_note: residents are taxed on income from sources in Moldova and on foreign income for work actually performed in Moldova
residency_rule: permanent residence in Moldova or >183 days in a calendar year
self_employed_regime: IT park residents — a single tax of 7% (covers personal income tax, social contributions and health insurance); sole proprietor 12%; retail 1% (min. MDL 3,000/year)
expat_regime: no
cbi_note: citizenship-by-investment programme abolished in 2020; now naturalisation only

pit_brackets_short: box 1: 8.10% (+27.65% national insurance = 35.75%)/37.56/49.5%; box 2: 24.5/31%; box 3: 36% on deemed income
foreign_income_note: residents are taxed on worldwide income; savings/investments — box 3 (36%)
residency_rule: by facts and circumstances (permanent ties: housing, family, work, registration); expats are residents when moving with family or for >1 year
expat_regime: 30% rule (expat scheme): up to 30% of salary tax-free for up to 5 years with a minimum salary per the norm; from 2027 — 27%; partial non-resident status abolished (transition period until end of 2026)
cbi_note: no citizenship/residence permit programmes for real estate purchase; citizenship by naturalisation

foreign_income_note: residents — on worldwide income; new residents — 4 years of exemption of foreign income (transitional resident)
residency_rule: >183 days in any 12-month period or a permanent place of abode; loss — absence of >325 days in 12 months.
self_employed_regime: no
expat_regime: transitional resident: foreign income is not taxed for 48 months (once in a lifetime); since April 2026 the status 'non-resident visitor' for digital nomads — up to 275 days in 18 months without residence when working for a foreign employer
cbi_note: residence permit by investment only (Active Investor Plus: from NZD 5 million, real estate does not count); citizenship by naturalization after permanent residence

pit_brackets_short: 22% general income + stepped tax 1.7/4/13.7/16.8/17.8% (total up to 39.8%); property tax ~1–1.1%
foreign_income_note: residents — on worldwide income; 22% includes the municipal share
residency_rule: >183 days in 12 months or >270 days in 36 months
self_employed_regime: no special regimes; self-employed social contribution 11%
expat_regime: PAYE for temporary non-resident workers: 25% flat (incl. social contributions) on income up to NOK 725,050, no deductions and no tax return
cbi_note: no citizenship/residence permit programmes for real estate or investment

pit_brackets_short: no personal income tax (neither federal nor Emirate-level)
foreign_income_note: no income tax; tax residency is needed for a residency certificate
residency_rule: main place of residence and centre of interests in the UAE, or ≥183 days in 12 months, or ≥90 days + UAE/GCC residence permit/citizenship + housing or work in the UAE
self_employed_regime: individual entrepreneurs pay corporate tax of 9% on turnover > AED 1 million (salary, personal investments and real estate income are not counted)
expat_regime: no (no tax); social contributions only for UAE/GCC citizens
cbi_note: residence permit only: 2-year investor permit via real estate; 10-year Golden visa from AED 2 million. Citizenship is not granted for real estate

pit_brackets_short: 8/9/10%; service income < PYG 80 million is not taxed; capital gains 8%
foreign_income_note: only Paraguayan-source income is taxed; foreign dividends, interest, rent — outside IRP
residency_rule: >120 days a year
self_employed_regime: IRP 8–10% on service income; simplified regimes (SIMPLE up to ~$330,000 turnover, max. ~3% of revenue — for EAS legal entities)
expat_regime: no (territorial system)
cbi_note: residence permit only: real estate from $200,000 → immediate permanent residence; citizenship by naturalisation after 3 years

pit_brackets_short: 12/32% (+4% solidarity surcharge above PLN 1 million); capital 19%
foreign_income_note: residents — on worldwide income
residency_rule: centre of personal/economic interests in Poland or >183 days in a year
self_employed_regime: flat 19% or ryczałt on revenue (12% for IT, 14% for a number of professions, etc.); + health contribution 4.9–9%
expat_regime: ulga na powrót: 4-year exemption up to PLN 85,528/year for those relocating (for foreigners — with 3 years of residence in the EU/EEA/Switzerland before moving, etc.)
cbi_note: no citizenship/residence permit programmes for real estate; citizenship by naturalisation

foreign_income_note: residents — on worldwide income
residency_rule: >183 days in any 12-month period or housing used as the main residence
self_employed_regime: simplified regime at turnover up to €200,000: 75% of service income is taxed (coefficient 0.75); social contribution 21.4%
expat_regime: IFICI (NHR 2.0; art. 58.º-A EBF, Portaria 352/2024/1): 20% on qualifying income and exemption of foreign income for 10 years - only for those working in eligible structures (science and teaching, R&D, certified startups, companies with a CAE from the list or exports ≥50%); category B (self-employment) - also only through such a structure; services to foreign clients are not covered (Ofício circulado 20276/2025). Self-employed with foreign clients: 12.5–48% on 75% of income + social contribution 21.4%; IRS Jovem up to 35 years; the old NHR closed in 2024
cbi_note: real estate excluded from the golden visa since 10.2023 (funds from €500,000); from May 2026 citizenship after 10 years (EU/CPLP 7), counted from issue of the residence permit card

pit_brackets_short: 10%; dividends 16%, capital gains 16% (through a broker 3/6%)
foreign_income_note: residents — on worldwide income (salary of Uruguayan citizens for work abroad is exempt)
residency_rule: domicile, centre of life interests or >183 days in any 12 consecutive months
self_employed_regime: PFA 10% (actual income or norma de venit) + CAS 25%/CASS 10%; micro-enterprise (SRL) 1% of turnover up to €100,000
expat_regime: no
cbi_note: no citizenship/residence permit programmes for real estate; citizenship by naturalisation

foreign_income_note: per dkdeniz: residents — on worldwide income; per tekce: foreign income is not taxed if not brought in — sources differ
residency_rule: >6 months in a year (continuous or with interruptions)
expat_regime: no
cbi_note: residence permit only: real estate of any value + income ~$10,000/year; TRNC citizenship not earlier than 7 years + Turkish; TRNC recognised only by Turkey, risk of Greek Cypriot land claims

pit_brackets_short: salary 10%; capital/dividends 15%; rent/royalties 20%; additional annual tax 10/15% on income >3/6 average annual salaries
foreign_income_note: residents — on worldwide income
residency_rule: ≥183 days in 12 months or centre of business and life interests
self_employed_regime: flat-rate: fixed tax+contributions (usually a few hundred € a month) with turnover < RSD 6 million/year; independence test
expat_regime: 70% reduction of the personal income tax and contributions base for 5 years for newly relocated experts (permanent contract, shortage qualification); up to age 40 an additional deduction in the annual tax
cbi_note: residence permit only: temporary residence on the ground of real estate ownership, proved by a land register excerpt (Ministry of Interior); citizenship by naturalization requires at least three years of uninterrupted registered permanent residence (Ministry of Foreign Affairs)

pit_brackets_short: 0% up to SGD 20,000, then 2/3.5/7/11.5/15/18/19/19.5/20/22/23/24%; non-residents: 15% on salary (or the scale, whichever is higher), 24% on other income
foreign_income_note: income received in Singapore or from Singapore is taxed; a resident's foreign income is not taxed (except that received through a Singapore partnership). Work physically performed in Singapore is Singapore income regardless of who pays. No local taxes.
residency_rule: 183+ days of presence or work in a calendar year; also admin. easements: 3 consecutive years, 2 years with 183 days, a work pass of 1+ year
self_employed_regime: no special regime: self-employed pay personal income tax on the general scale; CPF 20% (ceiling SGD 8,000/month) — only for citizens and permanent residents, foreigners do not pay CPF
expat_regime: no (there is no special regime for new residents; foreign income is not taxed anyway)
cbi_note: no citizenship for real estate. The investment route only leads to permanent residence (GIP): SGD 10 million into a business / 25 million into a fund / family office 200 million; citizenship — after permanent residence (min. 2 years, in practice 3–6), with renunciation of the previous citizenship

foreign_income_note: residents are taxed on worldwide income regardless of remittance to Slovakia; non-residents — only Slovak. No local income taxes. Dividends 7% (profit from 2025).
residency_rule: permanent place of residence, or 183+ days in a calendar year, or housing with the intention of living permanently
self_employed_regime: 15% rate for sole proprietors/companies with annual income (turnover) up to €100,000; otherwise the general scale
expat_regime: no
cbi_note: no citizenship or residence permit for buying real estate; citizenship — ordinary naturalisation

pit_brackets_short: 16/26/33/39/50% (thresholds €9,721 / €28,592 / €57,185 / €82,346); capital income, rent 25% (capital gains decrease with holding period to 0% after 15 years)
foreign_income_note: residents are taxed on worldwide income; non-residents — Slovenian only
residency_rule: permanent place of residence, or habitual place of stay / centre of vital interests, or 183+ days in the tax year
self_employed_regime: "normirani s.p.": 80% of standard expenses at revenue up to €50,000 (up to €120,000 with full insurance 9+ months), tax 20% on the remainder (≈4% of revenue) up to a €72,000 base, above 35%
expat_regime: from 2025: a 7% tax reduction on salary for 5 years for new residents up to age 40 with a salary of ≥2 average salaries, who were not residents for 2 years
cbi_note: neither citizenship nor residence permit for real estate. Citizenship — 10 years of residence (the last 5 continuous), with renunciation of the previous citizenship

pit_brackets_short: federal 10/12/22/24/32/35/37% + state/city tax 0–~14% (in 8 states, e.g. FL, TX, NV, WA-salary, there is no state tax)
foreign_income_note: citizens and residents (incl. green card holders) are taxed on worldwide income; citizens — even when living abroad (FEIE, foreign tax credit). Plus state/city taxes; 3.8% on investment income at high incomes.
residency_rule: green card, or the substantial presence test: 31+ days in the current year and 183 "weighted" days over 3 years (current + 1/3 of last + 1/6 of the one before)
self_employed_regime: no special regime: general scale + self-employment tax 15.3%; deduction of 20% of qualified business income (QBI)
expat_regime: no
cbi_note: there is no citizenship for real estate. Investment routes lead only to a green card: EB-5 $1.05 million ($800,000 in targeted areas, 10 jobs), “Gold Card” $1 million; citizenship after 5 years with a green card

pit_brackets_short: 12% residents (salary at the main place of work, after deductions); other income 15%; non-residents 20%
foreign_income_note: residents are taxed on worldwide income (per armenian-lawyer.com; PwC does not specify); non-residents — only Tajik
residency_rule: citizens of Tajikistan — always residents; foreigners — more than 182 days in any 12 consecutive months
self_employed_regime: simplified regime for sole proprietors (IE) with annual income up to TJS 1 million — 6% of income
expat_regime: no
cbi_note: no citizenship or residence permit by investment programmes; foreigners cannot own land (only buildings/lease). Naturalization — 5+ years of residence

foreign_income_note: residents pay tax on foreign income earned from 01.01.2024 when (in any year) it is brought into Thailand; income before 2024 is not taxed on remittance. The draft exemption for remittance in the same/following year was NOT adopted as of 09.2026. Work physically performed in Thailand is Thai income.
residency_rule: 180+ days in a calendar year (in total)
self_employed_regime: no special regime for freelancers — general scale
expat_regime: LTR visa: for Wealthy Global Citizen, Wealthy Pensioner and Work-from-Thailand Professional, foreign income is exempt even when remitted; Highly-Skilled Professional — 17% flat tax on Thai salary. Thailand Privilege — gives no tax benefits
cbi_note: there is no citizenship for real estate; foreigners cannot own land (only condominiums). Long-term visas: Thailand Privilege (650,000–5 million baht), LTR. Citizenship — via permanent residence + 5 years + Thai language

pit_top_threshold: TRY 5,300,000 (for salary; other income has different thresholds)
foreign_income_note: residents are taxed on worldwide income. NEW: law No. 7582 (Resmî Gazete 04.06.2026, art. 20/D GVK, effective from 01.01.2026) — 20 years of exemption of foreign income (salary abroad, business, dividends, interest, rent, pensions) for those who became residents and were not residents/taxpayers of Turkey for the 3 preceding calendar years; citizenship does not matter; foreign tax is not credited; inheritance at 1%. IMPORTANT: work physically performed in Turkey (remote work for a foreign employer, freelance for foreign clients) is, under the source rule (art. 7 GVK), considered Turkish income — under 20/D, in the opinion of consultants, it generally does not fall (awaiting secondary legislation). Salary from a foreign employer — self-declared on the general scale. Freelance export of services — see self_employed_regime. Dividends of a foreign company: 50% exempt with a share from 20% (from 2026, was 50%) and transfer to Turkey before the filing deadline (art. 22/4 GVK); the company must have its registered address and management centre outside Turkey.
residency_rule: lawful place of residence in Turkey or more than 6 months in a calendar year; exception — temporary projects and force majeure
self_employed_regime: Sole proprietor (IE) (şahıs şirketi) on the general scale; export of services (art. 89/13 GVK; presidential decision no. 11257 of 30.04.2026): from 01.01.2026 a 100% deduction (was 80%) of income from a closed list of services to foreign clients - architecture, engineering, design, software, medical reports, accounting, call centre, testing, certification, storage, data processing and analysis, education, healthcare; marketing, advertising and consulting are not on the list; all revenue must be transferred to Turkey before the filing deadline
expat_regime: law 7582 (2026): 20 years of 0% on foreign (non-Turkish) income for new residents who were not tax residents for 3 years; inheritance tax 1%. Active remote work from Turkey is usually not covered
cbi_note: real estate from $400,000 (valuation by a licensed appraiser, payment in foreign currency through a bank, a note in the TAPU prohibiting sale for 3 years); alternatives - deposit/government bonds/funds/pension $500,000 for 3 years. The programme is in operation (2026), processing time 4 months – 1 year (Kulaçoğlu). Dual citizenship is allowed; banks carry out enhanced checks of the source of funds. Residence permit by real estate - from $200,000 in all provinces since 16.10.2023

pit_brackets_short: 12%; dividends and interest of residents 5% (dividends of joint-stock companies exempt until 2028); employees of IT Park residents — 7.5%
foreign_income_note: residents are taxed on worldwide income; non-residents — only Uzbek. No local income taxes.
residency_rule: 183+ days in any 12 months beginning or ending in the tax period; or fewer than 183 days but more than in any other country
self_employed_regime: from 2026 the fixed personal income tax for sole proprietors (IE) is abolished; IEs and self-employed with turnover up to 1 billion soums — turnover tax 1% (Decree PP-247); general simplified turnover tax 4%; IT Park — benefits until 2028
expat_regime: no
cbi_note: residence permit only: purchase of property from $100,000 (regions) / $200,000 (Samarkand, Bukhara etc.) / $300,000 (Tashkent) — residence permit while the property is owned; "golden visa" $250,000. Citizenship — 5 years, with renunciation of the previous citizenship

pit_brackets_short: employment income: 0% up to 7 BPC/month, 10/15/20/22/25/27/31/36%; capital income 12%
foreign_income_note: Uruguayan-source income is taxed; work physically performed in Uruguay (including remote work for a foreign employer) is Uruguayan income (IRPF). Residents' foreign dividends/interest — 12%; from 2026 (law 20.446) also foreign rental income and capital gains (ficto is possible: effectively 1.8–2.4% of the sale price).
residency_rule: 183+ days a year (short trips do not interrupt) or the centre of economic/personal interests (family, main income); presumption with investments (real estate ~USD 560,000 + 60 days of presence, etc.)
expat_regime: tax holiday: year of move + 10 years of 0% on foreign capital income (IRNR option) with 183+ days or purchase of real estate >12.5 million UI (~$2 million) or investments; from 2026 onwards — 6% for 5 years or a fixed payment; employment income is not covered
cbi_note: residence permit/permanent residence only: pensioner visa (law 16.340) — passive income from $1,500/month + from $100,000 in real estate; citizenship — 3 years (family) / 5 years of actual residence

foreign_income_note: citizen residents are taxed on worldwide income; foreigners (resident alien) and non-residents — only on Philippine income. Work performed in the Philippines is Philippine income. For the digital nomad visa (EO 86, 2025) foreign income, according to available data, is not taxed, but the rules are not finalised
residency_rule: resident alien — lives without a fixed term of stay; foreigners >180 days a year — non-residents carrying on activity (scale)
self_employed_regime: option of 8% of gross revenue above PHP 250,000 (not a VAT payer, revenue up to PHP 3 million) instead of the scale
expat_regime: no (no special tax regimes; DNV: up to 2 years, income from $24,000/year from abroad, only for citizens of countries with reciprocity — list not published)
cbi_note: no citizenship for real estate; foreigners cannot own land (only condominiums). Investment visas SIRV/SRRV — residence permit only (from $75,000); citizenship — 10 years

pit_brackets_short: state 12.64/19/30.25/33.25/37.5% + municipal 4.7–10.9% (avg. 7.5%) + church 1–2.25% (for members); capital income 30% / 34% above €30,000
foreign_income_note: residents are taxed on worldwide income; non-residents — 35% on salary at source
residency_rule: a permanent home or habitual place of stay in Finland, or continuous stay of more than 6 months; Finnish citizens are residents for another 3 years after leaving
self_employed_regime: no special tax regime — general scale
expat_regime: foreign expert regime: 25% flat tax on Finnish salary for up to 84 months with a salary from €5,800/month
cbi_note: neither citizenship nor residence permit for real estate; citizenship — naturalisation (5/8 years)

pit_brackets_short: 0/11/30/41/45% (thresholds €11,600 / 29,579 / 84,577 / 181,917 per share) + surcharge 3–4% above €250,000/500,000 (single) + min. tax 20% (CDHR) for incomes >€250,000; social charges on capital 18.6%, flat tax 31.4%
foreign_income_note: persons with tax domicile in France are taxed on worldwide income unless otherwise provided by a DTT
residency_rule: one of: home/main place of stay in France, main professional activity in France, centre of economic interests
self_employed_regime: micro-entreprise: turnover ceiling €83,600 (services) / €203,100 (trade); social contributions 25.6% (liberal professions) / 21.2% (BIC services) / 12.3% (trade); optional versement libératoire 1–2.2% instead of income tax
expat_regime: impatrié (art. 155 B CGI): for those invited from abroad (not residents for 5 years) until the end of the 8th year — exemption of the relocation bonus (or 30%), salary for days worked abroad, 50% of a number of foreign passive incomes; limit of 50% of remuneration
cbi_note: neither citizenship nor residence permit for real estate; investor residence permit Talent — €300,000 into a business (not real estate); citizenship — 5 years of residence

pit_brackets_short: up to €60,000: 15–23%, above: 25–33% (rate chosen by the municipality; default 20/30%); capital/property income — final at flat rates
foreign_income_note: residents — worldwide income; non-residents — Croatian only; the local surtax (prirez) no longer exists, it is built into municipal rates
residency_rule: 183 days of presence in one or two calendar years, or housing owned/at disposal for ≥183 days in a row
self_employed_regime: paušalni obrt: turnover up to €60,000, tax 12% on imputed income (≈€203–1,080 per year) + contributions ~€291/month
expat_regime: Digital nomad residence permit (income from €2,540/month, 1 year with extension): income from foreign employers/clients is exempt from personal income tax; not available to EU citizens
cbi_note: no citizenship-by-investment programme. Residence permit only: owning real estate falls under exceptional other justified reasons for temporary residence ("enjoyment of own properties"), maximum duration of the first temporary residence permit is one year (Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs); stays for other purposes are not counted towards long-term residence (Ministry of the Interior)

pit_brackets_short: salary: 0% up to €700/month, 9% €700–1,000, 15% above; entrepreneurs: 0% up to €8,400/year, 9% up to €12,000, 15% above; + municipal surcharge of 13% of the tax (15% in Podgorica and Cetinje) → max. ~17.25%
foreign_income_note: residents — worldwide income, non-residents — only Montenegrin; other income 15%, gambling winnings 12%
residency_rule: domicile or centre of vital interests in Montenegro, or ≥183 days in a calendar year
self_employed_regime: entrepreneurs on their own scale 0/9/15% (tax-free €8,400 per year) + municipal surcharge
expat_regime: digital nomad visa (up to 2 years with renewal): income from foreign employers/clients is exempt from personal income tax and contributions (art. 32d of the personal income tax law); the programme end dates in 2026 are not confirmed
cbi_note: the citizenship by investment programme (development projects) was closed at the end of 2022, not resumed as of Aug. 2026. Residence permit only: real estate from €150,000, 1-year residence permit with extension, usually not credited towards permanent residence; citizenship — 10 years + language + renunciation of the previous one

pit_brackets_short: 15/23%; foreign dividends/bonds can be taxed separately at 15%
foreign_income_note: residents — worldwide income; no local income taxes
residency_rule: permanent residence in the Czech Republic or ≥183 days in a calendar year (days of entry/exit count)
self_employed_regime: paušální daň for sole proprietors (OSVČ, not VAT payers, income up to CZK 2 million): a single payment of tax + contributions — 9,984 CZK/month (up to 1 million), 16,745 (up to 1.5 million), 27,139 (up to 2 million); or flat-rate expenses 40–80%
expat_regime: no
cbi_note: no citizenship by investment; no residence permit based on real estate purchase either

pit_brackets_short: 0% up to 13.5 UTA (CLP 11.3 million), then 4/8/13.5/23/30.4/35/40% (Impuesto Global Complementario, AT 2026)
foreign_income_note: residents/domiciled are taxed on worldwide income, but foreigners for the first 3 years from entry pay tax only on Chilean income (SII may extend by another 3 years); no local income taxes
residency_rule: 6 consecutive months in a calendar year or >6 months over two adjacent years; domicile (intention to stay) may result in taxation from the date of entry
self_employed_regime: work under boleta de honorarios: 15.25% withholding in 2026 (credited against the annual tax); there is no special regime for freelancers
expat_regime: foreigners — only Chilean-source income for the first 3 years (extension up to 6 years by SII decision)
cbi_note: investment visa (temporary residence for investors): USD 500,000 or the equivalent in other currencies invested in producing goods or services (National Migration Service); citizenship by nationalisation after five years or more of residence for permanent residence holders (ChileAtiende)

pit_top_threshold: CHF 185,100 (single, federal; ~$230,000); above CHF 793,900 the overall rate is capped at 11.5%
pit_brackets_short: federal 0–13.2% (effectively max. 11.5%) + cantonal and communal tax (e.g. Zurich up to 13%×coefficient, Geneva up to 18%×coefficient); in total ~22–45% depending on the canton
foreign_income_note: residents — worldwide income and assets (wealth tax in the cantons); foreign real estate/PE are excluded from the base (with progression); 35% withholding on Swiss dividends/interest
residency_rule: intention to reside permanently; or 30 consecutive days with work; or 90 consecutive days without work
self_employed_regime: no special regime; self-employed pay both the employer and employee portions of contributions
expat_regime: lump-sum taxation based on expenses (forfait) for foreigners not working in Switzerland, for the first time or after 10 years of absence (abolished in ZH, SH, AR, BL, BS); deductions for seconded expats (housing, school, relocation) with a contract of up to 5 years
cbi_note: no citizenship by investment (naturalisation 10 years); purchase of real estate by foreigners is restricted by Lex Koller; a residence permit is possible via the lump-sum tax, not via real estate

pit_brackets_short: municipal ~32% (on average) on the whole base + state 20% above SEK 643,000; capital income — 30% flat
foreign_income_note: residents — worldwide income; non-residents (SINK) — 22.5% at source from 2026 (20% from 2027); the municipal rate varies
residency_rule: permanent residence/domicile, continuous stay >6 months or retention of a substantial connection (for former residents — the 5-year rule)
self_employed_regime: no special regime
expat_regime: tax relief for experts (expertskatt): 25% of remuneration is exempt from tax and contributions for 7 years; not a Swedish citizen, not a resident for 5 years before hiring, salary > SEK 88,800/month (2026), application within 3 months
cbi_note: no citizenship or residence permit for buying real estate

pit_brackets_short: 0% up to LKR 1.8 million (personal deduction), then 6/18/24/30/36% (bands of 1 million/0.5 million/0.5 million/0.5 million), Y/A 2025/26 and 2026/27
foreign_income_note: residents — worldwide income; income for services paid in foreign currency and remitted through Sri Lankan banks: after deducting 1.8 million — 6% on the next 1 million and 15% above
residency_rule: ≥183 days in any 12-month period overlapping with the tax year (1 Apr – 31 Mar)
self_employed_regime: no special regime; max. rate 15% for export of services for foreign currency (IT, freelance, BPO)
expat_regime: no (except the 15% rate on foreign-currency income from services)
cbi_note: no citizenship by investment. Residence permit only: condominium purchase visa from USD 75,000 (suburban areas, 5 years, extendable) / USD 150,000 (urban areas, up to 10 years) (Board of Investment of Sri Lanka); Golden Paradise Visa from a USD 200,000 deposit, valid 10 years (Department of Immigration and Emigration)

foreign_income_note: residents — worldwide income with credit for foreign tax; non-residents — 25% at source; no municipal income taxes (only patente $10–700 for sole proprietors)
residency_rule: >183 days (with interruptions) in a tax year or in a 12-month period within two years
self_employed_regime: RIMPE: negocio popular (income up to $20,000) — a fixed annual amount; emprendedor ($20,000–300,000) — $60 + 1–2% of gross income
expat_regime: temporary tax residence (from 2024): investment from $150,000 in real estate/business for 5 years + income from $2,500/month — for 5 years only Ecuadorian income is taxed
cbi_note: no citizenship by investment. Residence permit only: investor temporary residence visa for real estate, a fixed-term deposit or company shares from 100 SBU (unified basic salaries), visa valid 2 years (Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Human Mobility); permanent residence is open to holders of temporary residence of more than 21 months (Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Human Mobility); citizenship by naturalisation after at least three years of domicile on a permanent residence visa (Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Human Mobility)

pit_brackets_short: flat 22%; tax-free minimum €700/month (€8,400/year) for all from 2026
foreign_income_note: residents — worldwide income; no local income taxes; the planned increase to 24% did not take effect (EMTA: 22% in 2025–2026)
residency_rule: >183 days in any 12-month period or permanent residence in Estonia
self_employed_regime: entrepreneur account (ettevõtluskonto, LHV): 20% on receipts up to €40,000 per year without deductions; OÜ company — 0% on retained profit, 22/78 on distribution
expat_regime: no
cbi_note: no citizenship by investment; investor residence permit for a shareholder of a company registered in the Estonian Business Register who has invested at least EUR 65,000 in the activities of that company in Estonia (Police and Border Guard Board)
